subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The deep ocean is a type of environment characterized by especially extreme conditions.
• Water pressure in the deep ocean can reach a crushing 1,000 times greater than at sea level.
• Animals that have adapted to these conditions can survive in the deep ocean.
• During brief periods, some areas of the deep ocean can be warmed by hydrothermal vents to a relatively comfortable 68 degrees Fahrenheit.
• Around 2,000 different species of fish are able to live in the deep ocean.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize how extreme the conditions can be in the deep ocean. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Animals that have adapted to extreme conditions can survive in the deep ocean.
choices.B: Conditions in the deep ocean are especially extreme, with water pressure reaching a crushing 1,000 times greater than at sea level.
choices.C: There are around 2,000 different species of fish that can live in the deep ocean, where some areas can be warmed to a comfortable 68 degrees Fahrenheit.
choices.D: Along with animals that have adapted to the deep ocean's conditions, around 2,000 different species of fish can live in the deep ocean.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes how extreme the conditions in the deep ocean can be, noting that the conditions are especially extreme and describing the water pressure as "crushing."
